correctness.rationale: The unique-long-gap count is bijective for n<=2q+1 and yields the exact polynomial. For b_s=n*C(t,s-1)/C(n,s), successive ratios are decreasing and second differences nonnegative from s=3; displayed fully factored rational differences have nonnegative numerators when q>=t. Since (1-b_s)^2-(1-b_{s-1})(1-b_{s+1}) is the sum of those two nonnegative differences, normalized coefficients are log-concave. Endpoint s<=2 and terminal s>=t+2 are handled separately. The power-cycle closed-neighborhood correspondence is exact; 63+92 exhaustive finite comparisons and 13040 exact formula checks passed.

originality.rationale: The closest same-object 2024 paper proves domination-sequence unimodality and explicitly labels ultra-log-concavity Conjecture 1.8. The new normalized inequalities for the entire dense cyclic-block range do not follow from that weaker result. Its special n=2ell+2 polynomial and general recurrence are acknowledged prior, as is the standard hypergraph hitting-set interpretation. The 2026 general paper proves log-concavity for threshold graphs and normalized probability monotonicity, neither implying this theorem. value.rationale: The result is a direct infinite two-parameter partial resolution of a published 2024 ultra-log-concavity conjecture, strictly beyond the known unimodality theorem. The threshold n<=2q+1 is a natural sharp unique-long-gap boundary, and the normalized failure-probability convexity plus logconcavity establishes structural information for every coefficient simultaneously. The explicit formula and proof apply more generally to consecutive-block transversal systems; no paper-sized or downstream claim is required.
